Resolves #20223

🌿 *"To extend the Workstation, copy `createRoot`" is no longer advice anyone has to give.*

`Workstation.view.ViewportController` gains a `workspaceModule` config, defaulting to `Workstation.view.Workspace`. `createRoot` now builds the main workspace through a new `createWorkspace(config)`, which instantiates that class. An app that extends the Workstation can swap in its own Workspace subclass in two ways: by config (`controller: {module: ViewportController, workspaceModule: MyWorkspace}`) or in a controller subclass. Neither requires copying the hydration in `createRoot`.

Evidence: L2 (unit specs in Node) → L2 required (the config default and an override at the instantiation point).
agent-preflight: not hosted here; the engine's CI baseline runs on this PR.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `ViewportController.spec.mjs` › the root workspace defaults to Workstation.view.Workspace |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `ViewportController.spec.mjs` › an extending app swaps the root workspace class through the controller config; `createRoot` calls `createWorkspace`, the controller's only workspace instantiation (`Neo.create(` appears twice in the file: `TopologyLibrary` and `createWorkspace`) |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the two specs above |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/` (249 specs, green locally on this branch at `bcc162c1`) |

## Deltas from ticket
The instantiation moved into `createWorkspace(config)`, so a spec can pin it without the IndexedDB hydration that `createRoot` runs first. The existing spec stubs `createRoot` for the same reason.

## Test Evidence
All coverage runs in CI.
